quests.briefing: The knocking has become a line: an entire rival crew stands at the airlock, flags down, weapons slung, asking to come in, because their own shelter burned behind them, and the shelter watched the smoke for two days. The cost is not mouths; the cost is rivals, inside. The room has looked at the flags, and at the smoke.

stages.text: On the screen, flags down and weapons slung, and behind them the smoke the shelter watched for two days.

choices.text: Open up. Flags down, they come in.
Keep it shut. Rivals stay outside.

quests.briefing: The camera shows what the knocking sounds like this time: the sick, at the airlock, coughing into cloths, and the cloths are held up, because whoever is knocking knows what the shelter will ask. The sickness is legible at the door, and so is the cost. The infirmary has been asked to speak first, and the infirmary has said we have beds, and did not say how many.

stages.text: On the screen, the cloths are held up, and the infirmary says we have beds, and does not say how many, and the room hears both.

choices.text: Take them in. Quarantine and treat.
Keep it shut. The sickness stays out.

quests.briefing: The knocking is slow this time: the dying have come to the airlock, because someone told them the shelter buries its dead with names, and they want the names. The cost is small and the cost is everything. The room has been quiet a long time, and the knocking has gone on, slow, and nobody has called the vote, because nobody wants to be the one to say the word.

stages.text: The knocking is slow, and the room has been quiet a long time, and nobody calls the vote, because nobody wants to be the one to say the word.

choices.text: Open up. Give them the names.
Keep it shut. We cannot carry more.

quests.briefing: The dosimeter at the door has read the knock before anyone opened anything: whoever is out there is hot, and the reading is posted, and the room has read it, and the room knows what the reading means, and the knocking has gone on anyway, because whoever is out there knows what the reading means too, and has come anyway.

stages.text: The dosimeter reading is posted by the airlock, and the room has read it, and the knocking goes on anyway, and everyone knows what the reading means.

choices.text: Open up. Straight to the decon line.
Keep it shut. The reading is the reading.

quests.briefing: The knock is the one nobody believed: raiders at the airlock, weapons down, hands open, asking to come in, saying peace, and the word sounds wrong in their mouths, and they know it, and they have said it again anyway. The settlement they raided is the settlement voting. The room has looked at the hands, and at its own list of names.

stages.text: On the screen, weapons down and hands open, and the room looks at the hands, and then at the names on the wall, and then back.

choices.text: Keep it shut. Say the names instead.

quests.briefing: The final vote is not a knock, it is a policy: open doors, to all, from now on, because the shelter has decided what it is, and what it is is the place that opens. The cost is listed, and the cost is real, and the room has read the cost, and the room has read what it is, and the vote has been called, and the shelter has stood for it, because this one should be stood for.

stages.text: The vote is called, and the shelter stands for it, because this one should be stood for, and the airlock waits.

choices.text: Open the doors. All of them.
Keep the doors. Stay what we were.

quests.briefing: The surface is taking people, and the proposal starts with food: double rations for scouts, because the surface spends bodies and the shelter should repay. The cook has seconded the proposal before it was read, and the seconding has been logged, and the vote has passed on the sound of it.

stages.text: The cook seconds the proposal before it is read, and the seconding is logged, and nobody objects.

quests.briefing: The proposal continues: the best protective gear goes to the scouts, because they are the ones walking into what the gear is for. The gear inventory has been read aloud, and the best of it has been in command storage, and the room has noticed where it has been, and the room has voted to move it, and the moving has happened the same day.

stages.text: The gear inventory is read aloud, and the best of it has been in command storage, and the room notices where it has been.

quests.briefing: The proposal names a debt: hazard pay for scouts, in what the shelter has, which is rations and fuel and first pick, because the surface is paid in people and the pay should be visible. The pay scale has been posted, and the scouts have read it, and one of them has said it is not about the pay, and the room has raised the pay anyway.

stages.text: One of the scouts says it is not about the pay, and the room raises the pay anyway.

choices.text: Refuse. First pick is too much.

quests.briefing: The proposal reaches the planning: bad missions are to be aborted, and bad is to be defined by the scout in the field, because the field knows things the map does not. The operations office has gone quiet at this, because the operations office draws the maps, and the room has given the scouts the word, and the word is no.

stages.text: The operations office goes quiet, because the office draws the maps, and the room gives the scouts the word no.

quests.briefing: The proposal is weight: armed backup for every surface run, because the surface has started meeting scouts with numbers, and the shelter has been asked to arm the backup, and the armory has been asked what it can spare, and the armory has said what it can spare, and the room has voted to spend it.

stages.text: The armory says what it can spare, and the room votes to spend it, and the backup roster goes up the same hour.

choices.text: Refuse. The armory is the last line.

quests.briefing: The proposal is the one the scouts have been asking for without asking: retrieve the dead, because the surface has been keeping them, and the shelter has been letting it, and the letting has been a cost, logged in names the scout lead carries. The room has been shown the list, and the room has voted, and the vote has not needed a count.

stages.text: The list of names is shown to the room, and the room votes, and the vote does not need a count.

quests.briefing: The proposal is a rule: scout safety over salvage, always, and the rule is to be written into the orders, and the orders are to be signed with the rule visible. The operations office has been asked to rewrite the order forms, and the forms have been rewritten, and the rule is at the top, where it can be read before the quota.

stages.text: The order forms have been rewritten, and the rule is at the top, where it can be read before the quota.

choices.text: Put the rule at the top.
Refuse. The quota is the rule.

quests.briefing: The proposal is a refusal, written as a rule: suicide missions are refused, by the shelter, in advance, and the refusal is posted where the orders are drawn, so no one has to refuse them alone again. The scout lead has been asked to post it, and she has posted it, and has stood next to it for a while.

stages.text: The refusal is posted where the orders are drawn, and the scout lead stands next to it for a while.

choices.text: Refuse. Some orders must stay possible.

quests.briefing: The proposal is the one nobody drafted, so the scout lead drafted it: leadership takes the next surface risk, because risk should be known by the people who order it, and the room has read the roster, and the roster has the council's names on it, and the room has looked at the council.

stages.text: The roster has the council's names on it, and the room looks at the council, and the council looks at the roster.

choices.text: Refuse. The council stays under cover.

quests.briefing: The final proposal is a promise: absolute protection of the scouts, because they are the shelter's eyes, and the shelter has been spending them. The promise is written out, and it is signed by the whole room, because promises should carry everyone's name, and the scouts have been asked to sign last, because the promise is to them.

stages.text: The promise goes around the room for signatures, and the scouts sign last, because the promise is to them.

quests.briefing: Water is life, but it is also dignity, and the proposal starts there: reserves released for basic hygiene, because the shelter has been washing with rags, and the shelter has started to smell like what it has been through. The proposal is modest, and the vote passes quickly, and the showers run for one day, and the settlement stands in line with towels it had forgotten it owned.

stages.text: The showers run for one day, and the settlement stands in line with towels it had forgotten it owned.

quests.briefing: The proposal continues: reserves for laundry, because the shelter's clothes have been worn past wearing, and the smell is in the walls now, and the walls are where the shelter sleeps. The laundry list has been posted, and the wash day set, and the settlement has carried its clothes to the water in bundles, and the bundles have been heavier than anyone says.

stages.text: The settlement carries its laundry to the water in bundles, and the bundles are heavier than anyone says.

choices.text: Give the water for the wash.

quests.briefing: The proposal reaches comfort: warm water for washing that is not need, because the shelter has forgotten what comfort feels like, and forgetting is a cost too. The proposal is one paragraph, and the paragraph says hands, faces, and whatever else the heart asks, and the room has read that line twice, and the vote has passed without debate.

stages.text: The paragraph says whatever else the heart asks, and the room reads it twice, and the vote passes without debate.

quests.briefing: The proposal is the strange one: reserves for art, because the shelter's children have been asked to paint, and painting needs water for the colors, and the shelter has been asked what the colors are for. The answer has been given by a child, who said to make the walls not-walls, and the room has voted, and the colors have been mixed that afternoon.

stages.text: A child says the colors are to make the walls not-walls, and the room votes, and the colors are mixed that afternoon.

choices.text: Give the water for the colors.

quests.briefing: The proposal reaches the bay: reserves for hydroponic flowers, because the bay has been growing food, and the shelter has been eating, and the proposal asks what the eating is for. The flowers are to be planted in the middle row, where everyone walks, and the bay chief has been asked, and has said I have been saving seeds, which is how the room knows she has known all along.

stages.text: The bay chief says she has been saving seeds, and the room knows she has known all along, and the vote passes.

choices.text: Refuse. The middle row is for calories.

quests.briefing: The proposal names the animals: reserves for keeping the pets alive, because the shelter has animals, and the animals have been drinking from the same ration, and the proposal says to make it official. The animals have been counted, and the count has been read out, and the room has smiled at the count, because the count is absurd, and the room has voted yes anyway.

stages.text: The animal count is read out, and the room smiles, because the count is absurd, and the room votes yes anyway.

choices.text: Refuse. The animals share the ration.

quests.briefing: The proposal is the quiet one: reserves for the dying's last requests, because the dying have been asking for water, to wash, to drink, to hold, and the asking has been logged, and the log has been read to the room, and the room has not debated. The vote has passed, and the hospice has been given the key, and the key has not been asked back.

stages.text: The dying's requests are read out, and the room does not debate, and the hospice is given the key, and the key is not asked back.

quests.briefing: The proposal reaches the airlock: reserves for the refugees, because the ones taken in have been drinking last, and the proposal says first. The refugees have been told, and have not believed it, and the telling has been done again, slower, and the believing has happened the second time, and the line has been redrawn that day.

stages.text: The refugees are told the water is theirs first, and do not believe it, and the telling is done again, slower.

quests.briefing: The proposal has crossed into abundance: reserves for extra rations, because the shelter has been hungry so long it has forgotten what enough feels like, and the proposal says to remember. The ration board has been rewritten, and the new number has gone up, and the settlement has looked at the number, and the number has held, and the settlement has eaten.

stages.text: The new ration number goes up, and the settlement looks at it, and the number holds, and the settlement eats.

choices.text: Raise the ration. Feed them full.
Refuse. Enough is a number we cannot hold.

quests.briefing: The final proposal is the one the shelter has not let itself think, so the proposal thinks it: absolute abundance, for one day, because the shelter needs to know what it is working toward, and what it is working toward is a day without counting. The day has been set, and the settlement has been told, and the settlement has not believed it, and the day has come anyway.

stages.text: The day of abundance comes, and the settlement stands before the water, and does not count, and drinks.

choices.text: Refuse. Counting is what keeps us alive.

quests.briefing: The age of dictators is over, someone has said, and the saying has been written down, and the writing has been posted, and the first vote is called: work hours, binding, everyone votes. The ballot has been passed around, and the settlement has voted, and the count has been read out, and the count has stood, because the count is the shelter's.

stages.text: The count is read out, and the count stands, because the count is the shelter's.

quests.briefing: The vote continues: food rations, binding, because the ration is the shelter's life, and the life should be voted. The ration board has been put to the settlement, and the settlement has amended it, twice, and the amendments have been logged, and the board has gone up amended, and the shelter has eaten under its own law.

stages.text: The settlement amends the ration board twice, and the board goes up amended, and the shelter eats under its own law.

quests.briefing: The vote reaches the room itself: leadership appointments, binding, because the shelter has been governed by whoever was standing, and the standing should be voted. The candidates have stood, and the settlement has voted, and the count has changed the room, and the room has let itself be changed, because the vote is binding, and the binding is the point.

stages.text: The count changes the room, and the room lets itself be changed, because the vote is binding, and the binding is the point.

quests.briefing: The vote reaches the law: laws and justice, binding, because the shelter has been judged by whoever held the gavel, and the gavel should be voted. The laws have been read aloud, all of them, and the reading has taken a day, and the settlement has voted each one, and the ones that failed have been struck, and the shelter has watched its own laws be made.

stages.text: The laws are read aloud, and the ones that fail are struck, and the shelter watches its own laws being made.

choices.text: Refuse. Justice is not a headcount.

quests.briefing: The vote reaches the surface: expedition targets, binding, because the surface is where the shelter spends its people, and the spending should be voted. The targets have been posted, and the scouts have spoken first, because the scouts walk the targets, and the settlement has voted with the scouts' words still in the room.

stages.text: The scouts speak first, because the scouts walk the targets, and the settlement votes with their words still in the room.

quests.briefing: The vote reaches the stores: resource allocation, binding, because the stores are the shelter's body, and the body should be voted. The allocation has been put to the settlement, and the settlement has asked questions, many, and the questions have been answered, and the allocation has been voted, and the stores have been opened under the vote.

stages.text: The settlement asks questions, many, and the questions are answered, and the stores are opened under the vote.

quests.briefing: The vote reaches the outside: faction alliances, binding, because the alliances decide who the shelter is, and the who should be voted. The factions have been named, and the terms read, and the settlement has voted, and the alliance has stood or fallen by the count, and the shelter has known which, because the count has been read aloud.

stages.text: The terms are read, and the settlement votes, and the alliance stands or falls, and the shelter knows which.

quests.briefing: The vote is the big one: the ultimate fate of the bunker, binding, because the bunker is the shelter, and the shelter should decide if it stays. The question has been written out, and the question is do we stay, and the settlement has voted, and the answer has been read, and the answer has been the shelter's, and the shelter has stood with it.

stages.text: The question is do we stay, and the settlement votes, and the answer is the shelter's, and the shelter stands with it.

choices.text: Refuse. Fate is not a ballot question.

quests.briefing: The vote reaches the top: stripping the Overseer's power, binding, because the power has been held, and the holding should be voted. The Overseer has been asked to speak, and has spoken, and the settlement has voted, and the power has been stripped or held by the count, and the count has been read, and the room has watched the Overseer hear it.

stages.text: The settlement votes, and the count is read, and the room watches the Overseer hear it.

quests.briefing: The final vote is the one the shelter has been walking toward: absolute egalitarianism, binding, because the shelter has been voting itself into being, and the being is the vote. The proposal has been read, and the proposal says one voice, one vote, forever, and the settlement has voted, and the vote has passed, and the shelter has become the thing it voted for.

stages.text: The proposal says one voice, one vote, forever, and the settlement votes, and the shelter becomes the thing it voted for.

choices.text: Refuse. The shelter needs its structure.
